### 📚 Color-Coded Summary of Ida Fiyo Mntwana’s Activism

> **🔵 Blue – ANCWL (African National Congress Women's League)**  
> - After Madie Hall Xuma resigned in 1949, Ida Fiyo Mntwana became the **national president of the ANCWL**.  
> - She was more radical than her predecessor, organizing women in **demonstrations, strikes, and civil disobedience**.  
> - This role marked her early leadership in the women’s movement within the broader anti-apartheid struggle.

> **🔴 Red – ANC Executive Committee**  
> - In 1950s, Mntwana was **elected to the ANC Executive Committee**, showing her growing influence at the national level of the African National Congress.  
> - This placed her in a key decision-making position within the broader anti-apartheid movement.

> **🟡 Yellow – FEDSAW (Federation of South African Women)**  
> - In **1954**, Mntwana became the **first president of FEDSAW**, a pivotal organization uniting women across racial lines to resist apartheid laws.  
> - Led the **Germiston Women’s March on 26 August 1952** (note: date correction — this march predates her FEDSAW presidency, but still part of her early activism).  
> - Organized the **march to the Union Buildings on 27 October 1955**, with around **2,000 women** protesting pass laws.  
> - Was one of the **defendants in the 1956 Treason Trial**, a major political trial of anti-apartheid leaders.

> **🟢 Green – Congress of the People**  
> - Mntwana helped organize the **Congress of the People** in 1956.  
> - On the **second day of the congress**, police invaded the gathering, sparking conflict.  
> - **She calmed the crowd by singing a freedom song from the platform**, preserving the spirit and continuity of the event.  
> - This moment symbolized her leadership, courage, and commitment to peace amid protest.

---

### 🏁 Additional Notes (Not Organization-Specific)

- **Legacy & Recognition**:  
  - Mntwana is featured in **The Long March to Freedom** bronze statue project (National Heritage Monument), created by Sarah Lovejoy.  
  - In **August 2000**, she was cited as a **"torchbearer"** during Thabo Mbeki’s speech at the unveiling of the Women’s Monument.  
  - Posthumously awarded the **Order for Meritorious Service in Silver in 2003**.

---

### ✅ Why This Strategy Works

- **Visual Clarity**: Each organization is instantly identifiable by color, reducing cognitive load when reviewing timelines or events.  
- **Memory Enhancement**: Color associations strengthen recall — for example, “blue = ANCWL” helps you remember her early women’s leadership.  
- **Contextual Understanding**: You can now trace her evolving role — from women’s league to national leadership to cross-racial mobilization through FEDSAW and the Congress.

---

### 📝 Tip for Reviewing Future Documents

When reading about activists or leaders in multiple organizations, **always assign a color** to each group and **use it consistently** in your notes or summaries. This turns complex information into a visual, memorable framework.

---

🟢 **Final Takeaway**:  
Ida Fiyo Mntwana was a **radical, courageous, and unifying leader** — from the **blue halls of ANCWL**, to the **red decision-making of the ANC**, to the **yellow-led FEDSAW marches**, and finally, the **green peacekeeping at the Congress of the People**. Her legacy lives on in South Africa’s struggle
